findings: Before this edit retained exit_dispatch always touched Hub and took its mutex even after successful managed shutdown. A statically initialized always-lock-free atomic admission flag now precedes any Hub access in exit_dispatch and terminate_dispatch.

Only activate under the existing Hub lock opens admission. Only pause/finish of the exact current State closes the flag; an unpublished or previously finished contender cannot close another live registry route.

A dispatcher that read true still takes the old mutex, rechecks current/paused/finished, and owns its counted State lease. The flag is a closed-route fast path, not a wait/join proof or replacement for the existing active/control/drain checks.
Manual drain never uses the flag: paused exit callbacks remain drainable exactly once. Inactive terminate dispatch still aborts; no claim that the CRT abort implementation is lock-free.

Header documents the bounded guarantee. Added unexecuted scenario preserves a live owner across inactive close, verifies paused natural callbacks leave manual drain pending, and checks retained thunks and LastError after owner destruction. Existing active-lease/rebind/terminate scenarios remain registered.
Current common build already uses C++20 and includes these units. No ABI layout, vtable, export, startup ordering, loader hook definition or build-script change.
